lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 4: Adversarial Robustness and Generative Models

unit.name: The GAN generator-discriminator game
unit.description: Explains the original GAN setup with a generator that maps random code to images and a discriminator trained to classify real versus generated images.
unit.summary: GANs are introduced as a two-model adversarial training method: the generator is the model ultimately used, while the discriminator is used to train it [ts=3373s]. The generator maps a small random code z into a larger image, so its architecture must upsample from a low-dimensional input to a high-dimensional output [ts=3406s]. The discriminator alternates between generated images and real database images and learns binary labels, predicting fake as 0 and real as 1 [ts=3511s]. Training succeeds when the generator becomes realistic enough that a strong discriminator can no longer reliably distinguish real from fake [ts=3562s]. Gradients flow through the discriminator and back into the generator, making the simultaneous optimization of two networks a stability challenge [ts=3586s].

key_points.text: A GAN contains a generator G and discriminator D that compete during training.
The generator takes a random code z and upsamples it into an image.
The discriminator is a binary classifier that predicts fake generated images as 0 and real database images as 1.
Successful GAN training means G fools D so well that D cannot reliably tell generated and real images apart.
Gradient signals pass through D to update G, so training two networks simultaneously can be unstable.
